A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TraMark research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original accuracy and leakage-verification experiments, hyperparameter studies, attack evaluations and appendix experiments on watermark sources and client sampling.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds ImageNet-1k results, computational timing measurements and per-client accuracy analysis.

M1.justification: Warmup, magnitude-based parameter partitioning, masked aggregation, watermark injection and verification remain unchanged. The rewritten aggregation expression in Algorithm 1 is equivalent under the shared main-task parameters used in the described workflow. Output-class extension already appeared in v3 Appendix A.10.

E1.justification: v4 Appendix A.9 adds ImageNet-1k evaluation, extending the existing image-classification coverage. The four previous main-task datasets and MNIST, SVHN and WafflePattern watermark sources remain; the alternative-watermark study moves from v3 Appendix A.7 to Section 5.3.

E2.justification: The retained comparisons use the same methods, including FedAvg, WAFFLE and FedTracker. The new timing comparisons reuse these methods. Newly cited MFL-Owner is discussed as related work but is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: New evaluation settings include 100 clients, 60 training rounds and vit-base-patch16-224-in21k for ImageNet-1k. Timing evaluations distinguish watermark injection from aggregation plus injection plus verification. Previously stated benchmark training settings, attack procedures and MA/VR definitions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds per-client utility analysis to examine whether average accuracy conceals poorly performing client models (Appendix A.12), plus computational cost breakdowns. Existing warmup, partition-size, watermark-size, divergence and attack analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v4 Appendix A.12 newly specifies seed 0 for the per-client analysis and reports standard deviations across clients. These describe client dispersion, not uncertainty across repeated runs. The existing three-seed averaging practice and watermark-source t-tests remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v4 substantially extends the reported evidence with ImageNet-1k results of 77.80% MA and 100% VR, individual client accuracies, and timing results: TraMark takes 6.85 seconds for injection and 74.35 seconds including aggregation and verification (Tables 3 and 9). Table 1 changes the reported average VR from 99.17% to 99.58% and reports FedTracker's non-IID CIFAR-100 VR as 90%, replacing v3's checkmark meaning above 95%. Existing main-task accuracy values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–4, Problem 1 and the mask decomposition remain unchanged. v4 Appendix A.10 adds the probabilistic assertion that expected false-positive rate is 1/r for r output labels, without a derivation or stated probability assumptions. Neither version supplies a traceability guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same formalization, server-side black-box traceability and 0.54% average accuracy-drop contributions. The added conclusion sentence about parameter coupling and attack robustness restates an interpretation already present in v3 Section 5.2.

C2.justification: v4 substantially expands discussion of false positives, communication costs, client fairness and the trade-off between model anonymity and traceability (Appendices A.10–A.13). It replaces v3's general computational-overhead warning with separate injection and verification cost interpretations and stronger claims of negligible cross-silo overhead. Collusion and missing theoretical guarantees remain acknowledged.

D1.justification: v4 newly supplies code access information in the abstract and reproducibility statement, identifies the ImageNet-1k model and training setup, and reports computational timings. Appendix A.5 also corrects the stated A6000 memory from 49 GB to 48 GB.

R1.justification: v4 adds Gai et al.'s MFL-Owner and discusses its claimed generalization limitations, adds the ImageNet citation, and expands the critique of client-side watermark manipulation in RobWE. Most related-work positioning is retained; the ViT reference update identifies the same work.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized language edits, separates detailed studies into Section 5.3, moves the alternative-watermark study into the main text, and reorganizes the scalability and discussion appendices. Affiliation and conference statements are also updated, while most existing prose and the main narrative sequence remain.

P2.justification: The two-column document becomes a single-column conference layout with extensively resized, wrapped and relocated displays. v4 adds timing and per-client tables, changes VR presentation from symbols to percentages, and redraws plot axes and legends. Figure 1 gains a VR overlay whose underlying analysis was already shown in Figure 5.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3's largely qualitative overhead discussion and averaged utility reporting, v4 supplies measured costs, per-client results, an additional ImageNet-1k experiment and code access information. These improve transparency and practical assessment. The gain is limited: the new false-positive estimate is unsupported by derivation or testing, broad efficiency and privacy assurances remain only partly substantiated, and the acknowledged collusion and traceability-guarantee gaps persist.
